project.name: EKS Blueprints DevSecOps demonstration
project.scope: The EKS API, managed nodes, VPC and private service endpoints described by the selected pattern, plus the proposed delivery and application controls for one demo workload.

basis_legend.SOURCE_CONTRACT: The upstream pattern or a reviewed dependency describes the behavior. The resolved plan and runtime measurements are separate evidence.
basis_legend.PROPOSED_POLICY: A rule for the demonstration. Confirm the policy and actual implementation before making it a required check.

evidence_rule: Record which boundary a case actually reaches, the normal control, the negative case, and an observation independent of the code under test. Configuration, policy fixtures and deployed behavior have separate results. An unknown required value calls for review.

verification_status.source_review: Pinned upstream and 130 parsed source units linked to review decisions
verification_status.terraform_plan: Terraform mock apply PASS; 106 evaluated resources
verification_status.ci_and_runtime: Local CI PASS; hosted CI PENDING; deployed AWS/Kubernetes PENDING

source_inventory.decision: The module supplies the endpoint defaults. Inspect the effective resource in the plan.
Managed node placement affects both network isolation and image pulls.
Track node subnet routing and the subnet tags used to discover internal load balancers.
The upstream input is enabled. The demo proposes leaving the account's default VPC outside its Terraform ownership.
The ECR interface endpoints and S3 route table associations jointly support image pulls. Interface endpoints also inherit the endpoint security group.
Read the effective protocol, ports, sources and group attachment after module expansion.
The STS endpoint provides a network path. Workload trust and permissions are defined by the future demo resources.
The executable platform oracle checks the cluster version and required add-on assignments.

matrices.boundary: Terraform cluster configuration to the EKS add-on platform
matrices.obligation: The cluster uses the reviewed Kubernetes version and declares CoreDNS, kube-proxy and VPC CNI for the same cluster.

evidence.ci: Inspect resolved aws_eks_cluster and aws_eks_addon resources from Terraform evaluation. Compare the version against the separate demo policy.

variants.case: The reviewed version and three required add-ons are present for the demo cluster.
A controlled resource fixture omits CoreDNS.
A controlled resource fixture selects a version outside the reviewed baseline.

matrices.boundary: Deployment network and EKS nodes to the Kubernetes API
matrices.obligation: The Kubernetes API has private endpoint access enabled and public endpoint access disabled.

evidence.ci: Compare the resolved aws_eks_cluster VPC settings with the expected private and public flags.
evidence.runtime: Compare the deployed EKS endpoint settings with the plan and observe a successful authenticated read from the approved private network.

variants.case: Both resolved endpoint flags match the intended private configuration.
An offline plan fixture declares a public endpoint.
An offline plan fixture has no private endpoint.

matrices.boundary: EKS managed nodes to VPC subnets and external networks
matrices.obligation: Managed nodes use the pattern's private subnets and have no route to the internet or public IP assignment.

evidence.ci: Resolve node subnet placement and effective route table associations. For freshly mocked custom subnets only, resolve an omitted optional public IPv4 flag through the documented AWS creation default recorded in policy.json. Deployed values require direct observation.
evidence.runtime: Compare actual node subnet IDs, ENI addresses and effective route tables with the approved topology.

variants.case: Every node subnet resolves to an approved private subnet with private routes.
An offline topology fixture includes an internet egress route for a node subnet.
An offline topology fixture places a node group in a subnet that assigns public addresses.

matrices.boundary: Private EKS nodes to ECR registry services and S3 image layers
matrices.obligation: The node VPC has both ECR interface endpoints with private DNS and an S3 gateway endpoint associated with every node subnet route table.

evidence.ci: Compare endpoint type, VPC, DNS and route table associations in the Terraform plan with the managed node topology.
evidence.runtime: A fresh test node pulls a demo image digest from private ECR. Confirm the pull in Kubernetes events and confirm the node had no cached copy or internet route.

variants.case: ECR API, ECR registry and S3 associations cover the node subnets.
An offline plan fixture lacks private DNS for one ECR interface endpoint.
An offline plan fixture leaves a node route table outside the S3 gateway associations.

matrices.boundary: VPC clients to private AWS interface endpoints
matrices.obligation: The security groups attached to the interface endpoints admit HTTPS from the pattern's VPC CIDR and limit their inbound rules to that contract.

evidence.ci: Compare every effective endpoint group attachment and its resolved ingress permissions with the VPC CIDR resolved from the same plan.
evidence.runtime: Compare actual endpoint attachments and ingress permissions returned by AWS with the approved configuration.

variants.case: The effective ingress admits TCP 443 from the declared VPC range.
An offline plan fixture includes an ingress source outside that range.
An offline plan fixture attaches a second group with ingress beyond the endpoint contract.

matrices.boundary: Terraform ownership of the demo VPC to the account's default VPC
matrices.obligation: The demonstration manages its own VPC. The account's default VPC stays outside the demo's managed resources.

evidence.ci: Check whether the Terraform configuration or state would manage an aws_default_vpc resource, including when the proposed action is a no-op.
evidence.runtime: Review the demo state and the owning account's VPC inventory before treating the deployment scope as confirmed.

variants.case: The plan and demo state include only the dedicated demo VPC.
An offline fixture places the existing default VPC under the demo's management.

matrices.boundary: GitHub pull requests and release jobs to AWS deployment identity
matrices.obligation: PR validation has no AWS deployment credentials. Publication and deployment require the matrix gate and a manual main-branch release. Both AWS role trusts bind the exact repository and main ref.

evidence.ci: Check the workflow and environment rules together with the IAM trust conditions using synthetic job contexts.
evidence.runtime: Use the Actions job record and an AWS role session audit record from the isolated demo environment to confirm the authorized release.

variants.case: An approved release on an allowed ref meets the environment and role trust rules.
A PR validation job context is evaluated for deployment access.
A synthetic job context belongs to a different repository or environment.
A synthetic release job has an unapproved ref despite targeting the named environment.

matrices.boundary: Docker build inputs to exported application image
matrices.obligation: The published image omits build credentials from image configuration, history and every exported layer.

evidence.ci: Inspect the exported single-platform image archive, configuration and history for a deliberately issued synthetic marker. Include a clean-image control and fixture artifacts that contain the marker.

variants.case: The synthetic value was available during the build and is absent from the final artifact.
An offline image fixture contains the synthetic marker in its metadata.
An offline image fixture contains the synthetic marker in one exported layer.

matrices.boundary: Build, deploy and node identities to the ECR repository
matrices.obligation: The approved build identity publishes to the assigned repository. Nodes can pull the assigned image. Publishing is outside the node and deployment roles.

evidence.ci: Evaluate the role and repository policies against a small table of registry operations and repository identities.
evidence.runtime: Correlate successful authorized image publication and the fresh private pull with the actual AWS identities and repository.

variants.case: The build role has publish access to the demo repository.
The node role has pull access to the demo repository.
Evaluate publication permission for the node and deployment roles against synthetic policy inputs.
Evaluate the build role's publish permission for an unrelated repository in policy fixtures.

matrices.boundary: Approved Docker build to ECR artifact to Kubernetes deployment
matrices.obligation: The Deployment references the same repository and digest recorded by the approved release build.

evidence.ci: Compare the trusted release record, ECR image digest and rendered Deployment image independently. Use a single-platform demo image so the manifest digest comparison is unambiguous.
evidence.runtime: Record the running workload's image metadata and the approved descriptor it resolves to.

variants.case: The recorded digest, registry descriptor and Deployment reference agree.
The rendered Deployment fixture references a different digest or repository.
The rendered Deployment fixture references an image by tag alone.

implementation_inputs: Approved release metadata from the trusted build job

matrices.boundary: Approved deploy identity to Kubernetes deployment permissions
matrices.obligation: The deploy identity can perform the intended release actions only in the demo namespace. Cluster administration is outside its role.

evidence.ci: Compare the resolved EKS access entry and Kubernetes grants with the intended verbs, resources and namespace.
evidence.runtime: Record Kubernetes authorization decisions for scoped and out-of-scope actions in a test cluster.

variants.case: The identity can update its demo Deployment.
Evaluate update permission for a synthetic Deployment in another test namespace.
Evaluate permission for a cluster-scoped administrative action.

implementation_inputs: EKS access entry for the demo deploy role

matrices.boundary: Kubernetes service account to workload role to the demo AWS resource
matrices.obligation: The named service account obtains the dedicated read-only role and can read its assigned demo object. Other service accounts and unrelated objects are outside that grant. Demo object storage retains all four S3 public access restrictions. The private workload selects regional STS and has a private STS network endpoint.

evidence.ci: Evaluate the workload identity mapping, trust and permission policy using declared and unrelated synthetic identities and object references.
evidence.runtime: Confirm the role identity and read result in the test environment using only synthetic objects.

variants.case: The intended service account reads its assigned object with the workload role.
Evaluate trust for a different service account in the fixture.
Evaluate read permission for a different synthetic object in the fixture.
A controlled resource fixture removes a public access restriction from demo object storage.
A controlled resource fixture omits the regional STS endpoint required by the private workload.

implementation_inputs: scoped read permission for a synthetic S3 object

matrices.boundary: Client traffic to the demo Kubernetes Service
matrices.obligation: The demo application exposes a cluster-internal Service and no public application entry point.

evidence.ci: Inspect rendered Service and routing objects for reachable entry points targeting the demo workload.
evidence.runtime: Observe an approved in-cluster health request and check the deployed service and load balancer inventory for public routes to the workload.

variants.case: The Service resolves inside the cluster and has only the intended internal entry point.
An offline manifest fixture declares a public route to the demo Service.

implementation_inputs: Ingress and Gateway configuration for the demo workload

authoring: Read the scoped source and follow dependency references to the effective resource.
Write the obligation, positive and negative scenarios, and observable evidence.
Walk from each security-relevant source block and field back to its matrix or review decision.
Add executable checks and bind each scenario to its matrix ID in the CI implementation phase.
pull_request: Validate the catalog, source inventory and scenario bindings.
Map the changed files and the changed blocks or fields inside them to impacted matrices.
Review a new or unclassified security-relevant change and link it to an existing matrix, add a matrix, or record a justified decision.
Run the applicable scenarios for the change and publish outcomes with their evidence level.
workflow.manual_sensitivity: Manual-only source mutation for one matrix ID or the whole catalog. Build a passing current-source control, change one source file in a disposable copy, re-evaluate the changed Terraform/image/configuration domain, and require the same matrix oracle to return FAIL. Preparation errors and REVIEW are not detections. Preserve original source hashes and per-matrix evidence.

next_stage_inputs: Publish the project to the intended private repository and run GitHub Actions
Configure the real GitHub repository and AWS deployment identities before a manual release
Collect independent deployed AWS and Kubernetes observations
